chunks: Ali from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you enter the state of Ihram, avoid killing all animals, except the viper, the scorpion, and the rat, for they damage the water skins and burn down the houses of the people.

And as for the scorpion, the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) extended his hand to the stone, and a scorpion stung him, so he said: 'May Allah curse you! You do not spare the righteous nor the sinner.'
And the snake, if it intends (to attack) you, kill it; if it does not intend (to attack) you, do not intend (to attack) it.
And the vicious dog and the wild beast, if they intend (to attack) you, kill them; if they do not intend (to attack) you, do not intend (to attack) them.
And the treacherous black snake, kill it in all cases, and throw the crow and the buzzard upon the back of your camel.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What animals can a pilgrim in Ihram kill and which must they spare according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the reliable chain of Safwan and Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, establishes the principle of 'takhalluf' (removal of pests) during Hajj, balancing ritual purity with practical necessity. It distinguishes between 'muhibb al-bayt' (pests that damage property, like rats) which are always permissible to kill, and 'muharrif' (animals that attack, like snakes) where killing is conditional on their aggression, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on intent and harm. The inclusion of specific birds like the crow and kite highlights the detailed application of these rules to both terrestrial and aerial threats during the sacred state.

en.hubeali: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Sahzaan, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, and Safwan, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘When you wear Ihraam, so fear killing the insects, all of them, except for the snake, and the scorpion, and the rat, for these tear the water containers and burn down (the house) upon the people of the house. And as for the scorpion, so the Prophetsaww of Allahazwj extended hissaww hand to the tree, and a scorpion bit himsaww. So hesaww said: ‘May Allahazwj Curse you! Neither do you leave a righteous one nor an immoral one’. And the snake, when it intends (to attack) you, so kill it. But if it does not intend (to attack) you, so do not intend (to attack it)’. And the vicious dog and the wild animal, when they intend (to attack) you, so kill them. But, if they do not intend (to attack) you, so do not intend (to attack) them. And the treacherous black snake, so kill it upon every state. And the crow and the buzzard, pelt it upon the back of your camel’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from his father from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from ibn abu ‘Umayr and Safwan from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When you assume the state of Ihram, then he should stay away from killing all moving thins except a serpent, scorpions and rats because it weakens water containers and scorches a family.

About a scorpion it is notable that the Holy prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, once extended his hand into a hole for something and a scorpion bit him; and he (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘May Allah condemn you. You do not distinguish between sinful and sinless ones.’
If a snake attacks you, you can kill it, but if it does not attack, do not attack it.
If a biting dog or a beast attacks you [kill them] but if they do not attack you, do not attack them.
If it is the treacherous black snake, kill it in all conditions. If it is a crow or al-Hida’at (another kind of crow), shoot them (if they are) on the back of your camel.’”
